standard.coverage: Covered employers under this state's own act, which adopts or matches the federal rate.
standard.note: Georgia's OWN statutory minimum wage is $5.15/hr (O.C.G.A. 34-4-3), below the federal floor -- so every FLSA-covered employer in Georgia owes $7.25 and the $5.15 figure only ever binds employees the FLSA does not reach. A payroll system that reads 'Georgia: $5.15' off a statute table and stops there is wrong for essentially every real employer.

stateStatutoryRate.note: The state's own enacted figure, preempted by the FLSA for covered employers.

tipped.note: Matches the federal cash wage and tip credit.

youthAndTraining.label: Federal youth opportunity wage
youthAndTraining.eligibility: Employees under 20, first 90 consecutive calendar days -- 29 U.S.C. 206(g). Not a state figure; carried here because it is the only sub-minimum wage available in this state.

indexation.note: Not indexed; moves only if the legislature (or Congress) moves it.

sources.verifiedBy: Fetched and read directly this session. DOL's own state-by-state table is the spine of every standard rate in this database; where a state's own labor department was ALSO read directly, that source is listed too and wins on any disagreement (see South Dakota's tipped cash wage for the one case where they disagreed).

sources.verifiedBy: Fetched and read directly this session. Source of the combined rate / maximum tip credit / minimum cash wage triple and the 'tipped employee' monthly-tips definition for every state and territory in this database.

knownGaps: Georgia's own act exempts employers with five or fewer employees and those with under $40,000 in annual sales; those employees may still be FLSA-covered individually. Not modelled.
